Brief 096 · mocks for Sky (Glyph, 2026-11-04)

Mocks only: nothing in unity/ changed. Every frame is a real capture (the batch's own shots, 0.2.2xx) with the kit's own fonts, icons and plates on top, drawn from HTML by make/ (prep.py, render.sh, index.py). No image generator was used and nothing was spent. All words are placeholders for Fable. Times follow the shift at 5:30 (objective 1): chime 5:10, last chance 5:20, Popovic out 5:30, his car 5:50, with the rivals at 2:35.

In short. (1) The start is the book's Job page, with Begin where Back would be. (2) A Book key, bottom right, takes over the notes key. (3) The feed shows one crucial card at a time and keeps it until clicked. Everything else goes to the book's Journal, and a dot on the Book key says there's something new. (4) Rivals going for the held car get a card with its fix, and Go on the car's ring says who holds it and what to do.

1 · The start briefing is the book's Job page

What's on it, and where it comes from

  • Target, goal and fails: the book's job slot (text.json book.job), with the same folded "Ways to fail 9 ›". The hook moves to a short second line (Fable).
  • The two ways, with their conditions: book.job.needs, so they're open circles at the start and ticked live in play from the same slots. New words: "Before 5:30", "From 5:50", "The driver is turned by 5:20".
  • Who each way runs through: face cameos (Inez and the guard; the driver). A hover or click turns the street to them. These replace the stills.
  • The shared end (objective 3's line, for Fable): "Both end at our car: Popovic in · Go · the rest clear before the seal".
  • The clock: the book's track with the new times. The last station is "His car leaves 5:50", which is plainer than "Popovic at car".
  • The cell: four faces, name, job word and one line each. A face opens that agent's Cell page. Dropped: "Gives the rivals a false tip". The Scout's line is now "Watches from furthest; listens in."
  • The purse and Heat on the "Ways to fail" row, since §10 lists Heat on the briefing. Begin is the book's orange. The rail works, and People and Journal are dim until there's something in them.
What I keep and drop. I'd drop the five stills and the drawn plan. The frozen street is the plan and the stills, it's what you'll play on, and it needs no capture step: the Linux blank came from that step. I'd keep the faces, because a new player needs to know who each way runs through. One design and one data source mean Job in play and Job at the start are the same page. Begin closes it and the clock runs from the view behind it.

2 · A clickable book, and every key-only feature

Recommendation. The book key goes bottom right, with an icon and the word "Book", in the notes key's slot. The notes become the book's Journal, so nothing is lost, and the feed card sits right above it. It costs about +0.14 % of the screen at rest (104 × 40 against 36 × 36). The glyph is a stand-in that Vela or I would draw into icons/singles. J stays, and so do B (opens Job) and L (opens Journal).

3 · The feed and the Journal

How it behaves

  • One card at a time, bottom right, above the Book key. It stays until clicked, and a click shows the next ("1 of n ›"). The clock runs, nothing pauses, and there's no time limit, so nobody misses one. Today's version shows two beats at once for 4 s each (text.json less.feed: maxOnScreen 2, seconds 4), which is why it felt "so fast I hardly bother reading it".
  • The card is the kit's panel_dark plate: a badge or face on a disc, a title of 4 words or fewer, then where and when in one dim line. Only the rivals card carries a fix, as two small chips. Clicking the place pans there without dismissing the card.
  • Everything goes to the Journal, crucial or not. The Book key's dot means the Journal has rows you haven't seen. Opening the book stops the clock, so it's the place to read.
  • The Journal holds today's L history as rows: time, icon, what happened, place, and a turquoise dot for unread. The filters are today's (All, Crucial, Learned, Turned, City). A row opens to the scene's lines (speech in Barlow, with the speaker's cameo) and its result as icons. The face on the curve is who the row was about, and the line goes to where it happened, the same rule as the people pages.

The crucial list (proposal for you to judge in a build)

#WhenWhy it's crucial
1Alert goes upIt changes who notices what right now, so the plan has to change.
2One of ours is seen actingIt adds Trail and can start a report. You may need to stop or move.
3A report lands, or police are calledA clock starts: get away, or deal with it before they arrive.
4The seal startsThis is the hard deadline for Go. The countdown also stays under the clock.
5The rival car turns inOthers are after Popovic, and they can beat you to him or the car.
6Rivals start for our car (obj. 7)A held car means Go is refused. It's the one loss you can still head off, with a fix on the card.
7One of ours goes downYou lose what that agent can do. If it's the Enforcer, you lose the run.
8Popovic comes outThe door window closes and the pickup window opens.
9A turn landsA way in opens: Inez can be called, or the driver will bring him.
10A turn is refusedA way in closes or costs more. Change plans while there's still time.
11A body is found (my addition)Trail and Alert jump, and an investigation starts.

Journal only, never a card: Overheard lines and learned facts (Intel fills, the book's dot shows new) · acts finishing ("Looped", "Watched": the portrait's success beat and the busy chip already say so) · city chatter and scenes · the chime (sound and the clock) · rivals posting and parking · refusals (a pop at the click) · the cell's chatter (the ticker).

4 · Objective 7: guarding the held car

Recommendation. The card fires on Game.RivalsForCar (code rivals.for-car, one per beat, as the feed already dedupes) and stays until clicked or until no rival is still walking in (question 5). On the ring, Go stays at 12 o'clock once Popovic is aboard. While the car is held it's shut by shape (stripes and a lock, never a colour of its own), with one violet holder dot on the wedge. Its pill says what happened and who did it ("Go 🔒 held by" and a badge per holder), and the line under it gives the fix ("Step out and draw · or down them"). That follows §10's refusal rule: what happened, why, the fix. A click on the shut wedge pulses the holder marks, which is already in the GDD. Fable's book line ("while the car is held, someone guards it outside, gun drawn") teaches this before it costs.

These frames are borrowed from a 3:50 fight capture, with the marks painted on. In it the Enforcer is still carrying Popovic while the seat pips show him aboard, and the goal line still reads "Get Popovic to the car". Read the marks, not the story. Only one rival is near the car, so the pill says "held by" one, and the other two wear the car disc.

Open questions for Sky

1. Start page: drop the old briefing's stills and the drawn plan?
The old page (brief 070) had five close-up stills and a small plan. On Linux the stills came up blank, and they need their own capture step. The book shows the real street instead.
A) Drop both. Faces stay as cameos, and hovering a way or a face turns the street to the place (mock 1b). B) Keep the stills as a strip under each way. C) Keep a small plan inset.
Recommended: A. It's one data source with no capture step, and it shows the place where you'll actually play it.
2. The rivals' 2:35 on the start page: shown, or "?" until seen?
The built book shows "?" for the rival car until the cell sees it (its timeline has known: false). The old briefing told 2:35 up front, and your brief lists it.
A) Show 2:35 from the start on both the start page and the book. B) "?" until seen on both.
Recommended: A. The briefing has always told it, and one design needs one rule. Remember that seeds may move it.
3. Where the book icon sits
Today the notes (history) key is bottom right, and the feed stacks above it.
A) Bottom right, replacing the notes key, with the feed card just above and the "new" dot on the key. B) Top right, under the people discs.
Recommended: A. The new card and the dot are in the same place, and it adds about 0.14 % of the screen at rest.
4. Icon alone, or icon + the word "Book"?
Your complaint was that people can't find it. The Squad button already carries a word.
A) Icon + "Book" (mock). B) Icon only.
Recommended: A. It reads first time, and drops to icon-only later if it crowds.
5. Does a crucial card ever leave on its own?
You said cards "last until clicked". Some go stale: rivals turn back, or the police are already here.
A) A card that's no longer true drops into the Journal by itself. Everything else waits for a click. B) Every card waits for a click.
Recommended: A. A stale warning misleads, and a fair check shouldn't depend on clearing old cards.
6. Speed (= / −) and next event (N)
They are key-only today. You turned down skipping ("Syndicate with strategy").
A) No buttons. N is off in the player's build, and = / − stay as keys for testers. B) A speed button on the pill.
Recommended: A.
7. A menu without Esc
Esc is the only way to reach Options, Controls, Restart and Quit during play.
A) "Menu" as the last item on the book's rail. B) A small ≡ plate on the HUD.
Recommended: A. It costs the HUD nothing, and the book is one click away.
8. The order of queued cards
Several can arrive at once in a fight.
A) Most urgent first: seal > police > agent down > rivals for the car > Alert > seen > Popovic out > rival car > turned or refused > body found. B) Oldest first.
Recommended: A.

Evidence and limits

  • The key audit: every PlayAction traced with rg to where it's read, and every HUD element with a PointerDownEvent or ClickEvent listed (HudToolkit*.cs, Host*.cs). The file and line references are in the table.
  • Every HUD piece was checked cropped at 2x (2c, 2d, 2e, 3d, 4c). Two faults found and fixed: the card's count sat under a corner screw, and its badge crossed the rim.
  • HUD budget: not measured by tools/hud-budget, since mocks have no HUD layer. Worked out by hand: +0.14 % at rest (the Book key). The card is about 1.4 % while shown, against 22 % allowed with a card.
  • The frames are real captures with the HUD painted out where the page covers it. Soft smudges show where bubbles or the pill were removed (above Inez in 3c, the top of 1b).
  • New words for Fable: "Book", the card titles, the shared-end line, "The driver is turned by 5:20", "His car leaves", the Journal's subline, "Go · held by", "Step out and draw · or down them".
